subtopic: W4A16 group size / Metadata vs accuracy trade-off
learningObjective: Reason about the trade-off between W4A16 group size, quantization accuracy, and metadata bandwidth.
profileData:
W4A16 group-size sweep on LLaMA-7B (perplexity, WikiText-2; lower is better):
  group=32:   4.51   (metadata = ~0.5 bit/param equivalent)
  group=64:   4.55   (metadata = ~0.25 bit/param)
  group=128:  4.62   (metadata = ~0.125 bit/param)
  group=256:  4.85   (metadata = ~0.0625 bit/param)
stem: The perplexity trend above shows finer group sizes yield better accuracy but with rising metadata cost. Which is the correct reading of the trade-off?

options.text: Smaller groups give more scale factors per weight matrix, letting each group's scale track a narrower value distribution — more accurate but with higher metadata bandwidth (still small relative to the weights). The right choice depends on the accuracy budget and bandwidth headroom; group=128 is a widely-used default because it captures most of the accuracy at ~3% metadata overhead.
Smaller groups are always better because more scales mean more information; the metadata cost is negligible and never affects wall-clock.
Larger groups are always better because they mean fewer scales to load; the accuracy differences are measurement noise.
The perplexity trend is unreliable because group size cannot affect model output; the differences must be caused by different random seeds during quantization.

explanation: Finer groups (smaller group size) mean each scale factor covers fewer weight values, allowing tighter fit to local distribution — higher accuracy. But each scale adds metadata: at group=32 with FP16 scales, metadata is one FP16 per 32 INT4 values = 2/(32*0.5)=12.5% overhead on top of the INT4 storage; group=128 gives 2/(128*0.5)=3.125%; group=256 gives 1.5%. The observed perplexity curve captures this trade-off directly. Options B, C are absolutist; option D denies a well-established mechanism.

optionExplanations.B: Wrong: metadata cost is real, not negligible at small groups.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: accuracy differences are systematic, not noise.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: group size is a fundamental quantization parameter.

nonImplications: Does not imply group=32 is always preferable when accuracy is critical — kernel-side handling of many scales can add latency.
Does not imply group=128 is optimal for every model — larger or more sensitive models may benefit from smaller groups.

sourceRefs.locator: Group size ablations in AWQ paper
